settings.language.title: Application language

advanced.problem_chars.title: Problem characters
advanced.problem_chars.description: Problem characters do not replace the whole character set. They add weight to allowed characters where the most errors have occurred.
advanced.input.title: Input & connection
advanced.input.description: These settings control where the input is read from, whether the program tries to automatically find a Morsewurst device on serial ports, and whether an incomplete round is finished after a long pause.
advanced.input.use_telemetry_as_truth_hi: Recommendation: keep enabled. The round is scored from raw telemetry (actual key press timings). If disabled, the program uses USB HID keyboard input, which is not accurate enough for reliable scoring.
advanced.input.auto_connect_serial: Try to connect to serial port automatically
advanced.input.keyboard_description: With this setting, the computer keyboard acts as a virtual straight key. Key presses generate the same raw telemetry as a physical Morsewurst device.
advanced.input.keyboard_note: When enabled, the program uses the selected key as a virtual straight key, forces telemetry as truth, and disables automatic serial port scanning. Note that the keyboard is not a reliable or accurate Morse key.
advanced.input.auto_finish_description: This finishes the round if telemetry has arrived but the input remains too short, for example due to missing character gaps.
advanced.input.auto_finish_enabled: Finish incomplete round after a long pause
advanced.adaptive.title: Decoder & timing profile
advanced.adaptive.description: Morsewurst uses target WPM only as a starting estimate and learns the user's real rhythm from recent good rounds. Dot, dash and gap thresholds are not adjusted manually.
advanced.sound.title: Sounds
advanced.sound.description: These settings control Morsewurst sounds. The master sound switch acts as the main control. Individual event sounds can be enabled or disabled separately.
advanced.sound.practice_complete: Play sound when practice series completes
advanced.sound.serial_connected: Play sound when serial device connects
advanced.sound.serial_disconnected: Play sound when serial device disconnects
advanced.speed.title: Practice speed
advanced.speed.description: Target WPM defines the reference time against which the speed score is compared.
advanced.skill.title: Skill rating calculation
advanced.skill.description: Skill rating is calculated from recent sufficiently long rounds. Sufficiently long means at least {min_chars} target characters excluding spaces. The model considers effective WPM, accuracy, cleanliness, character mastery, coverage and timing.
advanced.effective_wpm.title: Effective WPM calculation
advanced.effective_wpm.description: Effective WPM is calculated from recent rounds that exceed the selected accuracy and cleanliness thresholds. The actual WPM is calculated from the target text's Morse units (PARIS standard) and round duration.
advanced.stats.title: General information history
advanced.stats.description: How many of the most recent rounds are used to calculate the historical averages in the General information panel on the main page. The calculation always uses the latest saved rounds up to this amount, regardless of round quality.
advanced.debug.title: Debug data
advanced.debug.description: The debug snapshot is saved only after the round ends. It does not write to disk during live Morse, so it does not interfere with timing measurement.
advanced.debug.save_snapshot_hint: When enabled, the latest round is always saved to latest_round_debug.json. The file is overwritten after each new debug round.
advanced.debug.save_history_hint: When history is enabled, each debug snapshot is appended to debug_history.jsonl. This allows individual rounds to be compared later.
advanced.debug.window_hint: In the debug window you can view the latest round, the full history in a clean format, or raw JSONL data.
debug_window.title: Debug data
debug_window.description: This shows the debug snapshot saved after the round. It contains the tone events received by the Python program, calculated gaps, decoder timing values, rescue decisions, and the final interpretation.
